The epitope of mAb F16 was determined based on reactivity with overlapping 15-mer linear peptides spanning the C-terminus of HA1 (HA1 300-329) and the extracellular HA2 region (HA2 1-185) of H5 VN/1194/04. F16 recognized residues in the fusion peptide.

The epitope of mAb F16 was deduced based on binding to a library of overlapping 26-mer helical coiled coil peptides spanning the helical HA2 sequence from HA2 38–125. Every fourth and seventh position of each 26-mer HA2 peptide was replaced by an Ile and Leu respectively, in order to maintain the helical coiled coil conformation of the peptide dimers in the hydrogel.

The epitope-specific mAb positively selected reactive fragments from a combinatorial HA (A/Anhui/1/05) antigen library displayed on the surface of yeast. The minimal sequence recognized by the mAb and four other mAbs was residues between I60 and G263 (F60–263 using H3 numbering) in the HA1 region. Mutations  E130D, S133L, K156T or N159K nearly abolished the ability of the mAb to neutralize the pseudovirus, indicating these are important residues for antibody recognition.

The epitope specific F005-126 antibody bound to HA from Influenza A virus (A/Fukuoka/C29/1985(H3N2)) expressed on 293T cells, but did not bind to HA from Influenza A virus (A/New Caledonia/20/1999(H1N1)). F005-126  bound weakly to a truncated H3 Fuk85 HA39-319 and did not bind to truncated H3 Fuk8544-309. The authors conclude the F005-126 epitope is on the globular head region (39-319). Escape mutant N285Y in HA H3 Aic68 was weakly recognized by F005-126 compared to the wild type H3 HA.

Epitope-specific mAbs LAH3, LAH5 and V15-5 bound to the LAH peptide (76-130 residue). LAH3 and LAH5 also bound to 30-residue overlapping LAH peptides 81-110, 86-115, 91-120, and 96-125, but not to 76-105 and 101-130. V15-5 bound to 91-120 and 96-125 and weakly to 86-115.

Epitope-specific mAbs LAH3, LAH5 and V15-5 displayed binding breath covering eight H3 HA proteins from H3N2 strains, isolated from 1968 to 2019 seasons. LAH5 moderately (and LAH3 weakly) cross-reacted with 4 of 8 H1 HAs in group 1, isolated between 1934 and 2007, but failed to react with H1 HAs from 2009 to 2019. MAb V15-5 did not react with any H1 HA tested.
